title: Repair Maintenance Hangar Facility Building 253 PSTE 172022
description: THIS IS AN AWARD NOTICE FOR SOLICITATION W50S9526BA003 / CONTRACT W50S9526CA002 This is a commercial service construction project in accordance with E.O.14271The USPFO for South Carolina intends to issue an Invitation for Bid to award a single firm fixed- price contract for services, non-personal, to provide all plant, labor, transportation, materials, tools, equipment, appliances, and supervision necessary to repair maintenance hangar to meet standard by utilizing conventional design and construction methods at McEntire JNGB. The scope of this project will consist of for adequate and efficient indoor workspace to maintain assigned and transient aircraft and provide organizational, administrative, component repair, logistical, tool storage, meeting, classroom, and other spaces. Work includes construction upgrades to the existing 65,000+ SF facility. Facility currently consists of hangar space, maintenance space, administrative, training, and storage spaces. Existing windows will be replaced throughout the facility with new energy efficient windows. Existing roof will be removed and replaced. The existing bi-parting sliding main hangar doors are to be removed and replaced with new doors. The existing unidirectional sliding Phase Dock hangar door is to be refurbished and receive new exterior skin. The existing facility shall be upgraded with new plumbing, mechanical, electrical, and fire protection systems with an emphasis on energy efficiency and conservation. The work is located at McEntire Joint National Guard Base near Eastover in Richland County, South Carolina. The award is anticipated to consist of the following line items (CLINs): CLIN 0001: Base Bid, in addition to the base work described above, the solicitation will include the following optional line items: CLIN 0002: Bid Option 1A: Eastern hangar trench drain and sewer modification, CLIN 0003: Bid Option 1B: Western hangar trench drain modification, CLIN 0004: Bid Option 2: Remove and replace existing generator, and CLIN 0005: Bid Option 3: Maintain temporary facilities through Phase 2. This project is set aside 100% for Small Business. The North American Industry Classification (NAICS) Code is 236220, with a size standard of $45,000,000.00. The magnitude of the project is between $10,000,000.00 and $25,000,000.00. The project is anticipated to occur in two phases with a total contract duration of 550 days after notice to proceed (NTP). The first phase includes demolition and renovations to the main hangar, shops opening to the rear of the main hangar, and the second floor organizational and admin space. The second phase includes renovations to the Phase Dock Hangar, the Fabrication Shop, and the Tire Room. No work shall begin on phase two until the government has fully accepted stage one and issued a separate NTP (this may not start immediately following stage one completion). *NOTE: If option(s) are unilaterally exercised within the timeframe noted in FAR 52.217-7 they shall be completed during performance of the base bid construction and will not extend total period of performance. title: Unaccompanied Enlisted Personnel Housing (UEPH), Joint Base Myers Henderson-Hall (JBMHH), Fort Myer, Virginia
description: Unaccompanied Enlisted Personnel Housing (UEPH), Joint Base Meyer-Henderson Hall (JBMHH), Virginia. The US Army Corps of Engineers, Baltimore District intends to solicit for an award to construct standard design barracks to include living quarter suites to accommodate 200 Soldiers, clothes, steam and barber rooms. Primary facilities include cybersecurity and antiterrorism/force protection (AT/FP) measures, building information systems, fire protection and alarm systems, intrusion detection system (IDS) installation, and energy monitoring control systems (EMCS) connection. Sustainability and energy enhancement measures are included. Supporting facilities including site development with demolition, utilizes and connections, steam for clothes pressing room, storm drainage, paving, parking, walkways, lighting, information systems, landscaping, and signage. Heating and air conditioning will be provided by a self-contained system. Measures in accordance with the Department of Defense (DoD) Minimum Antiterrorism for Building standards will be provided. Comprehensive building and furnishing related design service are required. Access for individuals with disabilities will be provided as appropriate. Facilities will be designed to a minimum life of 40 years in accordance with DoD?????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????s Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC 1-200-02) including energy efficiencies, building envelope and integrated building systems performance. Demolish 16 buildings at Joint Base Myer-Henderson Hall, VA (30,897 Total SF). Air conditioning (Estimated 420 Tons). The period of performance is 1460 calendar days from the Notice to Proceed. title: Global Distribution Expeditionary Contract
description: In accordance with RFO FAR 6.103-1, the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Distribution intends to issue modification P00024 against Contract SP330021D5002 on a sole source basis to Olgoonik Federal, LLC. This contract known as the Global Distribution Expeditionary Contract (GDEC) provides critical labor and distribution support for workload surges, unforeseen or unplanned requirements, contingency operations, humanitarian missions, labor augmentation, and special projects. The modification will increase the contract ceiling by $90,000,000.00, raising the total ceiling to $315,500,000.00. This increase is necessary because the current ceiling will be fully obligated prior to the end of the six month extension period, based on historical usage rates and projected surge and contingency requirements. The additional ceiling represents the minimum amount needed to maintain uninterrupted mission support.This action is being taken pursuant to RFO FAR 6.103-1(c)(2)(ii), as only the incumbent contractor, Olgoonik Federal, LLC, can provide the required services without unacceptable delays. Standing up a new contractor would require onboarding, security vetting, facility access approvals, training, and integration with DLA Distribution systems activities that cannot be completed within the required time frame. The incumbent currently maintains the necessary staffing, facilities, equipment, and materials to continue immediate performance.This temporary extension is required because follow on procurements the DLA Distribution Expeditionary Capabilities Contract (DECAP) and the DLA Distribution Labor Augmentation Contract will not be awarded in time to meet immediate and ongoing operational requirements.Without this ceiling increase and short term extension, DLA Distribution would not have a viable contract vehicle to support mission essential surge, contingency, humanitarian, or audit readiness requirements during the gap between the expiration of the current ordering period and the commencement of follow on contracts. The Justification and Approval document supporting this non competitive action will be posted to SAM.gov once fully executed.This notice is for informational purposes only. It is not a solicitation for proposals or an invitation for bids. The Government does not anticipate receiving responses to this announcement of a proposed non competitive action.

title: The Mission and Installation Contracting Command (MICC), Fort Campbell, KY, is issuing this Special Notice to identify small business concerns interested in receiving future request for quotations for various construction and related facility-support.
description: SPECIAL NOTICE Fort Campbell Operation and Maintenance, Army (OMA) Construction and Related Facility Support Requirements Contractor Repository � Fort Campbell, KY (Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 12.201-1(d) (DEVIATION 2026-O0028)) PURPOSE The Mission and Installation Contracting Command (MICC), Fort Campbell, KY, is issuing this Special Notice to identify small business concerns interested in receiving future request for quotations for various construction and related facility-support requirements at Fort Campbell, KY. In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 12.201-1(d) (DEVIATION 2026-O0028), the Government intends to establish and maintain a repository of interested and qualified small businesses concerns. The repository will be used to efficiently distribute future requirement-specific requests for quotations to firms that respond to this notice and represent that they can perform the applicable work. The Government�s objectives are to: I. Reduce administrative costs and procurement lead time; II. Improve opportunities for small business concerns; III. Promote efficiency and economy in contracting; and IV. Avoid unnecessary burdens for the Government and contractors. This Special Notice is not a solicitation, request for quotations or commitment by the Government to issue a purchase order (PO). The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with preparation or submission of a response to this notice. 1. Anticipated Requirements The Government anticipates requirements primarily associated with NAICS Code 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction, including repair, alteration, maintenance, minor construction, and related facility-support work. Although NAICS Code 236220 (Size Standard: $45.0 Million. Product Service Code (PSC): Z2JZ - Repair or alteration of miscellaneous buildings.) is identified as the primary anticipated NAICS code for this notice. Individual future requirements may require a different NAICS code, product service code (PSC), size standard, scope, licensing requirement, bonding threshold, or other requirement appropriate to the specific work. Anticipated work may include, but is not limited to: General construction, repair, and alteration of facilities; Carpentry, masonry, welding, roofing, painting, electrical, plumbing, and heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) work; Civil, site, drainage, earthwork, and related utility work; Demolition and removal services; Hoist and crane inspection, maintenance, repair, and related services; Environmental, energy-conservation, logistical, and other facility-support requirements; and Other construction or service requirements supporting Fort Campbell facilities and infrastructure. 2. Geographic Area Performance will occur at Fort Campbell, KY, (Zip Code: 42223) and may include associated facilities located within: Tennessee: Montgomery and Stewart County Kentucky: Christian and Trigg County 3. Acquisition, Eligibility, and Registration Requirements The Government anticipates executing future requirements through individual purchase orders (POs) on an as-needed basis. Individual POs are anticipated to range from $2,000 to $9,000,000. Each individual PO or associated request for quotation will specify the applicable statement of work, performance location, completion date or period of performance, submission instructions, evaluation criteria, and other terms and conditions. To be considered for future opportunities, interested contractors must meet and maintain the following requirements, as applicable to each individual requirement: Small Business Participation: This initiative is focused on expanding opportunities for small business concerns. The Government encourages participation from all small business socioeconomic categories, including Small Business (SB), Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB), 8(a) Business Development Program participants, Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone) small businesses, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB), and Women-Owned Small Businesses (WOSB). SAM Registration: Contractors must maintain an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) and possess a valid Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) to be eligible for award. Installation Access: Contractors must be able to obtain and maintain the personnel credentials, vehicle access, insurance, and other installation-access requirements necessary to perform work at Fort Campbell. Requirement-specific access instructions will be provided for each individual PO, as applicable. Insurance and Bonding: Contractors must be able to provide current and valid proof of general liability insurance and meet applicable bonding requirements at the time of award. Any required bid guarantees, performance bonds, payment bonds, or other insurance and bonding documentation will be identified in the individual request for quotation or PO. Inclusion in the contractor repository does not constitute prequalification, guarantee receipt of a future request for quotation, or guarantee award of a PO. 4. Repository Process and Future Requirement Notices This Special Notice will remain open for 12 months from the date of posting, unless cancelled earlier by the Government. The Government may renew or repost the notice annually, as needed. Firms responding to this notice may be included in the Government�s repository of interested contractors. Inclusion in the repository: Does not constitute prequalification; Does not establish a contract, blanket purchase agreement, ordering agreement, or other contractual instrument; Does not guarantee that a firm will receive a future requirement notice, be invited to quote, or receive an award; and Does not relieve a firm from meeting the terms, conditions, and evaluation criteria established for each individual requirement. When a requirement is identified that falls within the scope of this notice, the Government intends to distribute a requirement-specific notice by email to repository firms identified as potentially capable of performing that work. Each requirement-specific notice may include: A scoping statement or description of the requirement; Applicable NAICS code, PSC, and size standard; Site-visit date, time, location, and access instructions, if applicable; Submission instructions and proposal due date; Required statement of work (SOW), technical approach, pricing, or other quote content; Evaluation criteria and basis for award; and Any applicable bonding, licensing, insurance, safety, security, or other performance requirements. Site visits may be conducted for individual requirements. Attendance is not mandatory; however, attendance is strongly encouraged. The Government will evaluate quotations and make any award in accordance with the procedures, terms, and evaluation criteria stated in the individual requirement-specific notice. 5. Response Instructions Interested small business concerns should submit a capability statement by email to MICCIDEA@army.mil with the subject line: Response to Fort Campbell RFO 12.201-1(d) Contractor Repository � [Company Name] In addition to the email, please complete the repository form. The link (IDEAS Construction Repository Form) and a QR code have been provided. Responses should only include the following: I. title: RAPID (Robins Agile Practices for Infrastructure Development) at Robins AFB
description: SUBJECT: � Robins Agile Practices for Infrastructure Development (RAPID) Umbrella Program Notice (10 U.S.C. � 2808a Other Transaction Authority) 1. BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT (BLUF) The Department of the Air Force, specifically the 78th Civil Engineer Group (78 CEG) at Robins Air Force Base (AFB), Georgia, is publishing this Umbrella Program Notice to announce the establishment of the Robins Agile Practices for Infrastructure Development (RAPID) acquisition framework. Operating under the innovative statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a, RAPID seeks to completely modernize base infrastructure and execute facility repair and construction projects using flexible, commercial-style Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs). Traditional Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) rules do not apply, enabling the Air Force to engage directly with local, regional, and national commercial builders who have limited or no prior federal contracting experience. 2. PROGRAM STRUCTURE & TIMELINE Rather than a single, one-off project solicitation, this Notice establishes the RAPID Umbrella Program, which will remain active for one (1) full year from the date of this posting. During this 12-month period, the Government will periodically publish project-specific solicitations, referred to as Areas of Interest (AOIs), directly under this umbrella. Each independent AOI will outline: The specific facility construction, repair, or modernization project requirements. The exact response date, time, and instructions for submitting Solution Briefs. The collaborative delivery model designated for that project, such as Progressive Design-Build (PDB) utilizing open-book Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) pricing, or Build-Only (BO) commercial delivery. Program ParameterDetailsStatutory Authority10 U.S.C. � 2808a (Standalone Facility Construction or Repair Authority)Umbrella Active Period12 Months (Continuous Open Notice)Execution VehicleProject-Specific Areas of Interest (AOIs) & Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs)Key FlexibilitiesNo FAR boilerplate clauses, standard commercial accounting (No CAS), negotiable termsFollow-on AuthorityEligible for non-competitive, sole-source follow-on production construction under � 2808a(c) 3. ELIGIBILITY & PARTICIPATION The RAPID framework actively seeks to lower barriers to entry. Unlike prototype OTAs, 10 U.S.C. � 2808a carries no statutory Nontraditional Defense Contractor (NDC) prerequisites and zero cost-share mandates. Commercial general contractors, specialty trades, design-build firms, and joint ventures are all fully eligible and strongly encouraged to monitor this notice and participate. 4. ACTION REQUIRED FOR INTERESTED VENDORS Interested commercial builders and designers should take the following immediate steps to prepare for upcoming RAPID projects: Monitor This Posting: Bookmark this SAM.gov notice. All project-specific AOIs will be posted as amendments or linked notices here. Register on SAM.gov: Ensure your company has an active, completely free registration and Unique Entity ID (UEI) on SAM.gov. Form Teaming Alliances: Begin networking with regional design firms, general contractors, and trade subcontractors to build integrated design-build consortia capable of executing rapid, commercial-style projects.

description: The Marine Corps Installations Command National Capital Region - Regional Contracting Office (MCINCR-RCO), Quantico, VA, has a requirement for Information Technology Support Services for the United States Marine Corps Education Command (EDCOM). The Government intends to issue a single award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract, consisting of Firm Fixed-Price (FFP) Contract Line Items for services and Cost Reimbursement (CR) for travel. The contract will have a five-year ordering period, totaling $45M ceiling value. The proposed acquisition will be done as a 100% set aside to Women Owned Small Business. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 541512. The Government will solicit proposals utilizing commercial contracting under FAR Part 12 and FAR 15- Contracting by Negotiation. The Government intends to award a contract using best value trade-off procedures. The award will be issued on an all or none basis. This procurement will be solicited under solicitation M00264-26-R-0015, which will be posted via the Solicitation Module in the Procurement Integration Enterprise Environment (PIEE) website (https://piee.eb.mil) on or about 30 September 2026. It is the responsibility of the offeror to continually view the website for the solicitation and any amendments. Contractors interested in doing business with the Government must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) website accessed through https://www.sam.gov. Contractor must also ensure annual representations and certifications are current or complete them at the SAM website as well. All prospective offerors interested in submitting an offer must have a commercial and government entity code (CAGE code). The points of contact for this solicitation are Genia Fouts, Contract Specialist at genia.fouts@usmc.mil or Jeffrey A. Sisk Sr. Team Lead at jeffrey.a.sisk@usmc.mil or Contracting Officer Christian Hernandez at christian.hernandezsoto@usmc.mil. title: Pre-Solicitation Notice for Indefinite Delivery Contract (IDC) for Regional Dredge Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) - USACE Huntington District - W91237-26-R-A024
description: 1. CONTRACT INFORMATION: The contract consists of a base period of one-year with four option periods, one-year each for maintenance dredging and/or clearing and snagging services for Ohio River Government Lock facilities and Ohio River open channel areas (within commercial navigation limits) located in the geographical boundaries of the following U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Great Lakes and Ohio River Division Districts: Nashville (LRN), Louisville (LRL), Huntington (LRH), and Pittsburgh (LRP). There will be no site visit for this requirement. The award of a target of (3) Firm Fixed price Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity Multiple Award Task Order Contracts (IDIQ-MATOC) is anticipated. The contracts will be awarded to up to three (3) qualifying Offerors. The total capacity for the sum of all task orders issued under these contracts is a shared Not to Exceed (NTE) amount of $80,000,000.00. This announcement is open to all businesses regardless of size. The NAICS code for this procurement is 237990, which has a size standard of $37 million in average annual receipts. If a large business is awarded this contract, it must comply with RFO Clause 52.219-9 Alt II Small Business Subcontracting Plan, Alternate II. Solicitation documents will be available on or about October 02, 2026, and can be downloaded at https://www.sam.gov. 2. PROJECT INFORMATION: The primary objective of this contract is to provide maintenance dredging and/or clearing and snagging services for Ohio River Government lock facilities and Ohio River open channel areas (within commercial navigation limits) located anywhere within the geographical boundaries of the following Great Lakes and Ohio River Division Districts: Nashville (LRN), Louisville (LRL), Huntington (LRH), and Pittsburgh (LRP). This includes work on any navigable tributary of the Ohio River system.3. SELECTION CRITERIA: The selection criteria for this contract are listed below in descending order of importance. (a) Past Performance: Each offerors past performance will be reviewed to determine the recency of experience, relevancy of experience, and the quality of performance for an overall confidence assessment. (b) Small Business Participation Plan: Submissions must demonstrate the minimum requirements in sufficient detail for the level of proposed participation of small businesses in the performance of this acquisition. Offerors shall provide narratives for any element for which they cannot meet the minimum requirements. Failure to provide narratives will be interpreted as a lack of valid explanations to meet minimum requirements. Small Business Participation Plans containing details above and beyond the minimum requirements may be given greater consideration. (c) Price Reasonableness: Price reasonableness will be utilized in the evaluation of the firm-fixed price effort.4. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS: Proposers shall submit all documents electronically through PIEE Solicitation Module at www.piee.eb.mil. No paper copies, CD, DVD, thumb drives, email, or facsimile will be accepted. To be eligible for award, a firm must be registered in System for Award Management (SAM). Register via the SAM internet site at www. SAM.gov. Questions may be submitted to Amy L. Davis; amy.l.davis@usace.army.mil. Please note, as of April 2018, GSAs System for Award Management (SAM) system requires new registrations and renewals of existing registrations to submit an original signed notarized letter identifying the authorized Entity Administrator. The notarized letter is not to be submitted to the Huntington Contracting Office as it is not our requirement. Vendors are encouraged to check their entitys status in www.SAM.gov and plan accordingly. If the prospective contractor is not registered in the SAM database, the Contracting Officer will follow the procedures in FAR 4.1103. Contact the supporting Federal Service Desk at www.fsd.gov, or by telephone at 866-606-8220 (toll free) or 334-206-7828 (internationally) Monday through Friday from 8am to 8pm EDT, for free assistance. The SAM registration process may take several weeks to process once submitted. Please carefully consider this information when deciding to submit your proposal.

description: Dinamikus beszerzési rendszer (a továbbiakban: DBR) létrehozása megfúró bilincsek, megcsapolók beszerzésére. A beszerzendő termékek és azok jellemzői: Megcsapoló híd műanyag csövekre D63 – D315 mérettartományban, megfúró bilincsek azbesztcement, acél és öntvény csövekre DN50 – DN300 mérettartományban, a vonatkozó közbeszerzési dokumentumokban – különösen, de nem kizárólagosan az ajánlattételi szakaszokban megküldésre kerülő Műszaki leírásban és árazótáblában – foglalt. elvárt előírásoknak paramétereknek mindenben megfelelő termékek szállítása az ajánlattételi szakaszokban részletezettek szerint. A beszerezni tervezett termékek becsült mennyisége: 20 000 darab. Egy ajánlattételi szakasz útján egyszerre legfeljebb 105.000.000 Ft értékű terméket tervez beszerezni az ajánlatkérő. A mennyiség meghatározására kizárólag a Kbt. 107. § (2) bekezdésében előírtaknak való megfelelés érdekében került sor, az AK korábbi felhasználási tapasztalatai alapján, azonban e mennyiség lehívására az AK nem vállal kötelezettséget, az ajánlattételi szakaszok eredményeként ettől eltérő mennyiségű áru/termék beszerzésére is sor kerülhet. A jellemző időtartam egy ajánlattételi szakasz alapján negyedév, fél év vagy egy év. Egy évnél rövidebb vagy hosszabb időtartamra történő beszerzési is lehetséges az aktuális üzemi igények függvényében. A Dunántúli Regionális Vízmű Zrt., maga is mint jelen eljárás Ajánlatkérője a Kbt. 32. § (1)-(2) bekezdése alapján központi beszerző szervként került kijelölésre az alábbi ajánlatkérők által: ALFÖLDVÍZ Regionális Víziközmű-szolgáltató Zrt., ÉRV. Északmagyarországi Regionális Vízművek Zrt., DMRV Duna Menti Regionális Vízmű Zrt., Északdunántúli Vízmű Zrt., Tiszamenti Regionális Vízművek Zrt., Kiskunsági Víziközmű- Szolgáltató Korlátolt Felelősségű Társaság. A Dunántúli Regionális Vízmű Zrt. a DBR-t a fent felsorolt ajánlatkérő társaságok beszerzési igényének ellátására hozza létre. A DBR-t a fent felsorolt ajánlatkérő szervezeteken kívül az állami integrációban részt vevő víziközmű-társaságok vehetik igénybe. Az ajánlatkérő a közbeszerzési igényeket indokolt esetben - figyelemmel a szállítási helyekre, termékekre - társaságonként külön ajánlattételi felhívások útján is megvalósíthatja, amely keretében csak meghatározott termékek is beszerzésre kerülhetnek, azaz az AK egy ajánlattételi felhívás útján nem köteles valamennyi, a DBR-ben meghatározott terméket beszerezni. Az ajánlattételi szakaszokat a Dunántúli Regionális Vízmű Zrt. fogja központi beszerző szervként az egyes ajánlatkérők számára lefolytatni. Az ajánlattételi szakaszok eredményeként a szerződést az adott ajánlattételi szakaszban/adott ajánlattételi szakasz ajánlati részében megjelölt Ajánlatkérő fogja saját magára vonatkozóan megkötni. A DBR időtartama 48 hónap. Ajánlatkérő nem ír elő ajánlati biztosítékot. A részletes feltételeket a közbeszerzési dokumentumok tartalmazzák.

title: Auxiliary Chamber Miter Gate Fabrication for Captain Anthony Meldahl Lock and Dam
description: The Huntington District Corps of Engineers intends to award a contract for the fabrication of an Auxiliary Chamber Miter Gate for Captain Anthony Meldahl Lock and Dam. The contract will be a Firm Fixed Price Supply Contract. Performance will be the fabrication and delivery of one (1) miter gate two (2) leaves and appurtenant items. The contract will be awarded to the offeror whose proposal conforms to the solicitation and is within a technical/price competitive range, if established, as determined by the contracting officer and has been evaluated as the most advantageous to the Government, all factors considered. All responsive offerors will be evaluated utilizing the following technical factors: Qualifications and Technical Approach, Past Performance, Capabilities and Capacities. Solicitation documents will be available on or about 22 June 2026 online at https://www.sam.gov. To be eligible for contract award, a firm must be registered in the System Award Management (SAM). Register via the SAM website at https://www.sam.gov/portal/public/SAM. Questions may be submitted to Janessa Myers at janessa.k.myers@usace.army.mil. A NAICS Code of 332312 has been established for this solicitation. The size standard is 500. This procurement is a total small business set-aside.

title: American Academy of Orthopedic Surgeons EMS and EMT Training Curriculum Sole Source Notice
description: This notice serves to announce per FAR 5.1 and 5.2 that 772nd Contracting Squadron will award a sole source contract for AAOS authored Emergency Medical Responder, 8th Edition Premier Package, Emergency Care and Transportation for the Sick and Injured, 13th Edition Premier Package, and Advanced Emergency Care and Transportation for the Sick and Injured, 4th Edition Premier Package including online tools access including Navigate Premier Access, FISDAP Assessment EMT, and FISDAP Skills Tracker. These specific materials are required per Air Force policy to be used for all education and training certification courses for all Air Force Fire and EMS personnel. The sole source award is being done under the authority of FAR 12.102(a), as it has been deemed that only one source is available to meet this specific requirement due to copyright restrictions of the materials and ownership and control of the online tools. The Government will award a sole source contract to Jones and Bartlett Learning LLC 25 Mall Rd, Burlington, Massachusetts, 01803.The applicable NAICS code for this acquisition is 513130 and the size standard is 1,000 employees. The acquisition will be awarded as a commercial service using Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services under the authority of FAR part 12.This notice is not a request for competitive quotes. Questions concerning this notice can be addressed to the attention of Nathan Pennington or David Koenig by email at nathan.pennington.3@us.af.mil david.koenig.2@us.af.mil

title: Repair Maintenance Hangar Facility Building 253 PSTE 172022
description: THIS IS AN AWARD NOTICE FOR SOLICITATION W50S9526BA003 / CONTRACT W50S9526CA002 This is a commercial service construction project in accordance with E.O.14271The USPFO for South Carolina intends to issue an Invitation for Bid to award a single firm fixed- price contract for services, non-personal, to provide all plant, labor, transportation, materials, tools, equipment, appliances, and supervision necessary to repair maintenance hangar to meet standard by utilizing conventional design and construction methods at McEntire JNGB. The scope of this project will consist of for adequate and efficient indoor workspace to maintain assigned and transient aircraft and provide organizational, administrative, component repair, logistical, tool storage, meeting, classroom, and other spaces. Work includes construction upgrades to the existing 65,000+ SF facility. Facility currently consists of hangar space, maintenance space, administrative, training, and storage spaces. Existing windows will be replaced throughout the facility with new energy efficient windows. Existing roof will be removed and replaced. The existing bi-parting sliding main hangar doors are to be removed and replaced with new doors. The existing unidirectional sliding Phase Dock hangar door is to be refurbished and receive new exterior skin. The existing facility shall be upgraded with new plumbing, mechanical, electrical, and fire protection systems with an emphasis on energy efficiency and conservation. The work is located at McEntire Joint National Guard Base near Eastover in Richland County, South Carolina. The award is anticipated to consist of the following line items (CLINs): CLIN 0001: Base Bid, in addition to the base work described above, the solicitation will include the following optional line items: CLIN 0002: Bid Option 1A: Eastern hangar trench drain and sewer modification, CLIN 0003: Bid Option 1B: Western hangar trench drain modification, CLIN 0004: Bid Option 2: Remove and replace existing generator, and CLIN 0005: Bid Option 3: Maintain temporary facilities through Phase 2. This project is set aside 100% for Small Business. The North American Industry Classification (NAICS) Code is 236220, with a size standard of $45,000,000.00. The magnitude of the project is between $10,000,000.00 and $25,000,000.00. The project is anticipated to occur in two phases with a total contract duration of 550 days after notice to proceed (NTP). The first phase includes demolition and renovations to the main hangar, shops opening to the rear of the main hangar, and the second floor organizational and admin space. The second phase includes renovations to the Phase Dock Hangar, the Fabrication Shop, and the Tire Room. No work shall begin on phase two until the government has fully accepted stage one and issued a separate NTP (this may not start immediately following stage one completion). *NOTE: If option(s) are unilaterally exercised within the timeframe noted in FAR 52.217-7 they shall be completed during performance of the base bid construction and will not extend total period of performance. description: BPA Call Order Exceeding $25,000 Synopsis Requisition 1174591 The USDA Forest Service Land Management is issuing this synopsis/solicitation notice as a means of complying with the USAD's policy in the Contracting Desk Book, SUBPART 413.3- SIMPLIFIED ACQUISITION METHODS, 413.303 Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs). The USDA FS intends on awarding a competitive BPA Call Order against LMIR BPA for 127EAT26Q0090- Airport BAR- Rare Plant Surveys, Cleveland National Forest The Land Management Integrated Resources BPA (LMIR) is a National BPA that consist of a large variety of work including Professional Services, Natural Resources Restoration, Engineering, Project Management, NEPA, Communications, and more. The BPA can be utilized on all Forests and Grasslands and is available for all federal agencies to utilize. This is not a solicitation. Any changes to the Call Order RFQ shall also be emailed to those companies listed on the BPA. This requirement will be competitively awarded as a BPA Call Order against the aforementioned multiple award schedule BPAs continuously solicited on the Government Point of Entry (GPE) at: SAM.gov. The government will not provide feedback or evaluations to companies regarding their submissions in response to this notice, however, the LMIR BPA is an open continuous BPA that allows us to accept responses for the life of the BPA. Search "Contracts" on sam.gov using solicitation number "12363N23Q4023". title: Hungary – Taps, cocks, valves and similar appliances – DBR - Különféle golyóscsapok beszerzése
description: Dinamikus beszerzési rendszer (a továbbiakban: DBR) létrehozása különféle golyóscsapok beszerzésére. A beszerzendő termékek és azok jellemzői: Hagyományos golyóscsap, kombinált golyóscsap, megfúró golyóscsap, a vonatkozó közbeszerzési dokumentumokban – különösen, de nem kizárólagosan az ajánlattételi szakaszokban megküldésre kerülő Műszaki leírásban és árazótáblában – foglalt, elvárt előírásoknak paramétereknek mindenben megfelelő termékek szállítása az ajánlattételi szakaszokban részletezettek szerint. A beszerezni tervezett termékek becsült mennyisége: 25.000 darab. Egy ajánlattételi szakasz útján egyszerre legfeljebb nettó 272.000.000 Ft összegű terméket tervez beszerezni az ajánlatkérő. A mennyiség meghatározására kizárólag a Kbt. 107. § (2) bekezdésében előírtaknak való megfelelés érdekében került sor, az AK korábbi felhasználási tapasztalatai alapján, azonban e mennyiség lehívására az AK nem vállal kötelezettséget, az ajánlattételi szakaszok eredményeként ettől eltérő mennyiségű áru/termék beszerzésére is sor kerülhet. A jellemző időtartam egy ajánlattételi szakasz alapján negyedév, fél év vagy egy év. Egy évnél rövidebb vagy hosszabb időtartamra történő beszerzési is lehetséges az aktuális üzemi igények függvényében. A Dunántúli Regionális Vízmű Zrt., maga is mint jelen eljárás Ajánlatkérője a Kbt. 32. § (1)-(2) bekezdése alapján központi beszerző szervként került kijelölésre az alábbi ajánlatkérők által: ALFÖLDVÍZ Regionális Víziközmű-szolgáltató Zrt., ÉRV. Északmagyarországi Regionális Vízművek Zrt., DMRV Duna Menti Regionális Vízmű Zrt., Északdunántúli Vízmű Zrt., Tiszamenti Regionális Vízművek Zrt., Kiskunsági Víziközmű- Szolgáltató Korlátolt Felelősségű Társaság. A Dunántúli Regionális Vízmű Zrt. a DBR-t a fent felsorolt ajánlatkérő társaságok beszerzési igényének ellátására hozza létre. A DBR-t a fent felsorolt ajánlatkérő szervezeteken kívül az állami integrációban részt vevő víziközmű-társaságok vehetik igénybe. Az ajánlatkérő a közbeszerzési igényeket indokolt esetben - figyelemmel a szállítási helyekre, termékekre - társaságonként külön ajánlattételi felhívások útján is megvalósíthatja, amely keretében csak meghatározott termékek is beszerzésre kerülhetnek, azaz az AK egy ajánlattételi felhívás útján nem köteles valamennyi, a DBR-ben meghatározott terméket beszerezni. Az ajánlattételi szakaszokat a Dunántúli Regionális Vízmű Zrt. fogja központi beszerző szervként az egyes ajánlatkérők számára lefolytatni. Az ajánlattételi szakaszok eredményeként a szerződést az adott ajánlattételi szakaszban/adott ajánlattételi szakasz ajánlati részében megjelölt Ajánlatkérő fogja saját magára vonatkozóan megkötni. A DBR időtartama 24 hónap. Ajánlatkérő nem ír elő ajánlati biztosítékot. A részletes feltételeket a közbeszerzési dokumentumok tartalmazzák.

description: MARKET SURVEY CAPABILITY ASSESSMENT Reliability and Probability Training (FAA28335) for Flight Standards and Aircraft Certification Airworthiness Inspectors/Engineers NO PHONE CALLS PLEASE. ALL QUESTIONS MUST BE EMAILED TO THE CONTRACT SPECIALIST CONTACT INFORMATION BELOW. This is a market survey issued to identify sources for a Firm-Fixed Price Indefinite Delivery/Requirements Type Contract for the acquisition of Reliability and Probability Training (FAA28335) for Flight Standards and Aircraft Certification Airworthiness Inspectors / Engineers employed by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). The contractor is to provide Reliability and Probability Training to FAA Airworthiness Inspectors / Engineers. The contractor may provide this training through their standard courses offered to the public, other Government agencies or by submitting courses solely intended for FAA inspectors. The FAA estimates this course to provide approximately 72 hours of instruction and class size should not exceed a maximum of 12 students. The purpose of this survey is to solicit statements of interest and capabilities from all businesses that are interested in and capable of providing the Reliability and Probability Training for Flight Standards and Aircraft Certification Airworthiness Inspectors / Engineers. In order to make the determination, the FAA requires the following from interested vendors in accordance with the attached Performance Work Statement (PWS): 1. Geographic area where training will be provided; 3. Expected approach � Respondents must provide their strategy for accomplishing this work. The principle North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this effort is 611519 Other Technical and Trade Schools, with a size standard of $21 million. The responses to this market survey will be used for informational purposes only. This is not a Screening Information Request or Request for Proposals of any kind nor is the FAA seeking or accepting unsolicited proposals. The FAA will not pay for any information received or costs incurred in preparing the response to the market survey. Therefore, any cost associated with the market survey submission is solely at the interested vendor�s expense. At this time the nature of the competition has not been determined. The FAA may decide to do a full and open competition or set aside all or part of the procurement for small businesses or eligible socially and economically disadvantaged business that are certified by the SBA for participation in the SBA�s 8(a) Program. The purpose of this market survey is to solicit statement of interest and capabilities for small businesses, service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses, 8(a) certified firms, and all other business types and sized, capable of providing specified Course Instruction. This market survey is also being conducted in order to obtain the information necessary to determine whether adequate competition exists to set-aside the competition among small businesses, service disabled veteran-owned small businesses or 8(a) certified firms. If applicable, interested firms which are SBA 8(a) certified are required to submit a copy of the SBA 8(a) certification letter. All responses to this market survey must be received by 5:00 p.m. CST, September 21, 2026. All submittals should be submitted by email to Federal Aviation Administration Kiara.J-CTR.Murry@faa.gov NOTE: This original announcement was posted on SAM.gov. title: LOWER BRULE NORTH SHORELINE STABILIZATION AND ECOSYSTEM RESTORATION, ELEMENT 2
description: On or about 6 October 2026, the Government intends to issue the Invitation for Bid (IFB) for LOWER BRULE NORTH SHORELINE STABILIZATION AND ECOSYSTEM RESTORATION, ELEMENT 2. The IFB will close on or about 10 November 2026. This is a 100% Small Business Set-Aside. Sit Visit: A Site Visit is scheduled for 28 October 2026. Additional information regarding the site visit will be provided in the solicitation in Section 00 21 00. Project Description: Element 2 of the project includes the construction of a 100-foot-wide riparian planting bench, a gravel maintenance path along the entire reach, and the creation of a 200-by-1,500-foot island within Reach 4 of the lake, in water up to three feet deep. The island will be planted with cottonwood trees and other culturally significant vegetation. To protect the lakeward side of the island from wind, wave action, and ice erosion, a riprap revetment will be installed. The sheltered open water area between the island and the shoreline is anticipated to naturally evolve into approximately 5.17 acres of emergent wetland. Additionally, this measure will result in the creation of roughly 32 acres of riparian habitat. DO NOT submit requests for plans and specifications. See Obtaining Solicitation Documents below. Completion Date: The Contractor will be required to commence work upon receipt of contract award and complete the work 450 days after receipt of Notice to Proceed. This is subject to change after IFB issuance. Provisions will be included for liquidated damages in case of failure to complete the work in the time allowed. Performance and Payment Bonds will be required. Estimated Construction Costs: The estimated construction cost of this project is between $10,000,000 and $25,000,000. NAICS Code: The Primary North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code anticipated for solicitation is 237990, Heavy and Other Civil Engineering Construction, with a size standard for Small Business of $45M. description: ARCHITECT-ENGINEER INDEFINITE DELIVERY/INDEFINITE QUANTITY MULTIPLE AWARD TASK ORDER CONTRACT FOR GENERAL DESIGN AND OTHER RELATED SERVICES WITHIN THE BOUNDARIES OR ASSIGNMENTS OF MISSISSIPPI VALLEY DIVISION, UNITED STATES ARMY CORPS OF ENGINEERS Solicitation (Synopsis) Number: W912P826RA012 Set-Aside Code: Unrestricted with a Partial Small Business Set-Aside Product Service Code: C219 - Architect and Engineering - General North American Industrial Classification System Code: 541330 - Engineering Services 1. CONTRACT INFORMATION: These services are being procured in accordance with 40 United States Code, Chapter 11, Selection of Architects and Engineers Statute, Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) Part 36. Firms will be selected for negotiation based on demonstrated competence and qualifications for the required work stated in this synopsis. This is not the Request for Proposal. Interested firms shall respond by submitting one Standard Form (SF) 330 listing their qualifications. North American Industrial Classification System Code is 541330, which has a size standard of $25,500,000 in average annual receipts. This Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) announcement is Unrestricted with a Partial Small Business Set-Aside pool. The resulting task orders will be negotiated Firm Fixed-Price for General Design and other related services. Multiple contract awards are anticipated, with a performance of five years, with four negotiated rate escalations each year after the initial first year. The total MATOC shared pool capacity shall not exceed $90,000,000 or five-year duration, whichever comes first. The minimum guarantee throughout the five-year contract is $1,000. Responding firms must address each evaluation criteria in the appropriate sections of the SF 330 for the prime contractor as well as all subcontractors and consultants. If subcontracted, clearly indicate what part of the scope they will be performing. To be eligible for the contract award, the firm must be registered in the Department of Defense (DoD) System for Award Management (SAM). Register via the SAM Internet site at https://www.sam.gov. For contractors requiring Common Access Cards (CAC) or contractors requiring unescorted access to USACE controlled property for greater than six (6) months the Centralized Suitability Service Center (CSSC) requires a T1 Background Investigation to be completed. Should a task order require a T1 Background Investigation it will be specified. The primary purpose of the proposed contract is to provide A-E General Design and other related Services anywhere within the boundaries or assignments of Mississippi Valley Division. 2. PROJECT INFORMATION: A-E and related services are to be accomplished through individual Task Orders, which shall consist of the following comprehensive scope tasks and requirements: (a) Core Engineering, Design, and Project Documentation: The work will involve investigations, comparisons, data evaluations, analyses, designs, water quality analyses, technical writing, and drafting for: Engineering Documents: Preparing Design Documentation Reports (DDRs) geotechnical reports, feasibility studies, plans and specifications, Operation, Maintenance, Repair, Replacement, and Rehabilitation (OMRR&R) manuals, value engineering, or other technical engineering documents. Design, Modeling & Drafting: Civil design, hydraulic design, hydrologicanalysis, sediment transport, coastal engineering, structural design, geotechnical design, mechanical design, electrical design, architectural design, naval architecture, project management, building and civil information modeling (BIM/CIM), and CAD drafting. Engineering Support During Advertisement (EDA): Preparing amendments to the advertised plans and specifications and updating the BIM/CIM as warranted by comments received from prospective bidders. Engineering Support During Construction (EDC): Attending pre-construction conferences; responding to contractor requests for information (RFIs) and clarifications; reviewing submittals from the construction contractor; and performing monthly or bi-weekly site visits (or visits at critical times) to witness construction practices, observe site conditions, and document implementation of the design from the designer's perspective. Levee Safety & Structural Periodic Inspections: Performing detailed, systematic technical inspections and evaluations of the safety, stability, and operational adequacy of levees and civil works structures. Support Services: Surveying and the use of aerial mapping are required to support this work. (b) Required Disciplines & Professional Qualifications: The assembled team must demonstrate professional qualifications, education, training, licensing, certification, professional registration, overall relevant experience, and longevity within their disciplines and firm. Key design personnel must include: Engineering: Structural, Civil, Hydraulic (including hydrologic analysis, sediment transport, and coastal engineering), Geotechnical, Mechanical, Electrical, Corrosion, Environmental, and Cost Engineering. Scientific & Applied Fields: Hydrologists, Geologists, Architects, Naval Architects, and Surveyors. Geospatial & Technology Specialties: Geospatial Information Systems (GIS) Mapping and Analysis, Drafting via Computer-Aided Design (Autodesk), 3D Modeling CAD consisting of Building Information Modeling (BIM), and Civil Information Modeling (CIM), and professional Project Management. (c) Types of Features & Project Scopes The work may involve existing and new projects at any design stage, involving new or existing structures, including: Hydraulic Structures: Locks, floodgates, floodwalls, levees, navigation structures, drainage canals and structures, pumping stations, and prestressed/post-tensioned concrete structures. Marine Structures: Bulkheads, dolphins, fenders, guide walls, jetties, or shoreline protection. Highway & Infrastructure Work: Roads, ramps, bridges, utility relocations, and buildings (such as warehouses, pump houses, or offices related to the structures above). Risk Reduction & Environmental Projects: Flood risk management, hurricane and storm damage risk reduction projects, non-structural techniques (including elevation), freshwater and sediment diversion projects, environmental infrastructure projects, and other multi-purpose projects. (d) Specialized Civil, Structural, Geotechnical, & Surveying Tasks: The work may involve the following detailed types of related analysis, modeling, and field work: Modeling & Structural Analysis: 3D modeling of buildings, structures, sites, and horizontal construction features; civil/site work design; structural design; planning; program and project management; finite element modeling; frame analysis; pile group analysis; and drainage analysis. Contract Package Development: Development of plans and specifications, Design-Build Requests for Proposals (RFPs), and real estate rights-of-way (ROW) drawings. Field Investigations & Testing: Hazard Toxic Radioactive Waste (HTRW) investigations; architectural treatments; landscaping; performing soil borings and soil testing to determine soil properties; and providing boring logs in accordance with USACE New Orleans District geotechnical criteria. Analytical Calculations & Engineering Evaluations: Developing pile capacity curves; bearing capacity analysis; cantilever retaining or floodwall analysis; temporary retaining structure design; time-settlement projections with lift schedules; soil pressures; seepage and dewatering analysis; stability analysis for levees using Spencer's Method and/or Janbu�s Method (including reinforced embankments, dikes, and other earthen structures); bank stability analysis; slope stability analysis for revetments, channels, and excavations; stability analysis of floodwalls (T-walls, I-walls, L-walls); downdrag and settlement analysis; numerical model

description: *****Solicitation Notice Update to Post the Bid Abstract on 25 August 2026*****. **Amendment 0002- This amendment is to: A. Provide DQM Pipeline Dredge Specifications for Small Business dated 04 August 2023, D. Provide Final Specifications and Final Plans dated August 2026, E. The project consists of using a hydraulic cutterhead pipeline dredge in North East River to remove material to its authorized depth of 7 feet (plus two feet of allowable over depth). Up to 100,000 cubic yards of silty to sandy material are to be dredged. Material will be transported via pipeline to the existing upland placement site. Pipeline distance will be approximately 6 miles from the furthest dredging location. The pipeline will travel through the North East River, up Stony Run creek, and over tidal and nontidal wetlands to reach the existing upland placement site. The dredging window is from 16 October 2026 to 15 February 2027; this is the only period of time dredging is allowed in the North East River. The estimated magnitude of construction is between $1,000,000.00 and $5,000,000.00. The construction duration will be approximately 120 calendar days from the Notice to Proceed. title: Global Distribution Expeditionary Contract
description: In accordance with DLAD 17.96 and RFO FAR 6.103-1, the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Distribution intends to issue a modification to Contract SP330021D5002 on a sole source basis to Olgoonik Federal, LLC. This contract known as the Global Distribution Expeditionary Contract (GDEC) provides critical labor and distribution support for workload surges, unforeseen or unplanned requirements, contingency operations, humanitarian missions, labor augmentation, and special projects. The modification will extend the ordering period by six (6) months through 31 March 2027, and contain a six (6) month option period through 30 September 2027, if necessary. This modification will also increase the contract ceiling by $100,000,000.00, raising the total ceiling to $415,500,000.00. This bridge action is necessary as DLA Distribution does not have any other contracts in place that provide for warehouse and distribution support for humanitarian, contingency, labor augmentation, audit readiness changes, or other unplanned requirements, both CONUS and OCONUS. This interim, short-term action is required because the follow-on procurement the DLA Distribution Expeditionary Capabilities Contract (DECAP) and the DLA Distribution Labor Support Services Contract will not be operational or awarded in time to meet immediate and ongoing operational requirements. This action is being taken pursuant to RFO FAR 6.103-1(c)(2)(ii), as only the incumbent contractor, Olgoonik Federal, LLC, can provide the required services without unacceptable delays. Standing up a new contractor would require onboarding, security vetting, facility access approvals, training, and integration with DLA Distribution systems activities that cannot be completed within the required time frame. The incumbent currently maintains the necessary staffing, facilities, equipment, and materials to continue immediate performance. A Justification and Approval document supporting this non competitive action will be posted to SAM.gov once fully executed. This notice is for informational purposes only. It is not a solicitation for proposals or an invitation for bids. The Government does not anticipate receiving responses to this announcement of a proposed non competitive action.

title: Poland – Portable computers – Dostawa laptopów na rzecz sądów powszechnych
description: 1. Przedmiotem postępowania jest ustanowienie Dynamicznego Systemu Zakupów (zwanego dalej DSZ) dla udzielania zamówień na dostawy laptopów (zwanych dalej sprzętem) na rzecz sądów powszechnych, Krajowej Szkoły Sądownictwa i Prokuratury i Centrum Zakupów dla Sądownictwa Instytucja Gospodarki Budżetowej, zwanych łącznie Jednostkami, będącymi nabywcami dostaw w ramach DSZ. Wykaz Jednostek stanowi Załącznik nr 9 do SWZ. Przedmiotem zamówienia w ramach DSZ jest dostawa laptopów wraz z zapewnieniem usług gwarancyjnych tego sprzętu. 2. Przedmiot zamówienia w ramach DSZ został podzielony sześć Kategorii: a) Kategoria 1: Laptop typ 1 - standardowy w szacowanej ilości 535 sztuk w całym okresie obowiązywania DSZ (Kategoria 1 dotyczy jednorazowych zamówień w maksymalnej ilości do 50 sztuk włącznie); b) Kategoria 2: Laptop typ 1 - standardowy w szacowanej Ilości 10 154 sztuk w całym okresie obowiązywania DSZ (Kategoria 2 dotyczy jednorazowych zamówień w ilości powyżej 50 sztuk); c) Kategoria 3: Laptop typ 2 - ponadstandardowy w szacowanej Ilości 173 sztuk w całym okresie obowiązywania DSZ (Kategoria 3 dotyczy jednorazowych zamówień w maksymalnej ilości do 50 sztuk włącznie); d) Kategoria 4: Laptop typ 2 - ponadstandardowy w szacowanej Ilości 3 285 sztuk w całym okresie obowiązywania DSZ (Kategoria 4 dotyczy jednorazowych zamówień w ilości powyżej 50 sztuk); e) Kategoria 5: Laptop typ 2, wersja 1 - ponadstandardowy w szacowanej ilości 682 sztuk w całym okresie obowiązywania DSZ (Kategoria 5 dotyczy jednorazowych zamówień w maksymalnej ilości do 50 sztuk włącznie); f) Kategoria 6: Laptop typ 2, wersja 1 - ponadstandardowy w szacowanej Ilości 1 025 sztuk w całym okresie obowiązywania DSZ (Kategoria 6 dotyczy jednorazowych zamówień w ilości powyżej 50 sztuk); 3. Zamawiający dopuszcza możliwości składania wniosków o dopuszczenie do udziału w DSZ na jedną, kilka lub wszystkie Kategorie. 4. Opis minimalnych parametrów sprzętów objętych DSZ w ramach danej Kategorii oraz minimalny wymagany okres gwarancji dla sprzętów, określony został w Załączniku nr 2 do SWZ – Opisie przedmiotu zamówienia. 5. Celem ustanowienia DSZ jest kwalifikacja podmiotowa Wykonawców, zdolnych do wykonania przedmiotowego zamówienia w okresie obowiązywania DSZ w oparciu o ustalone w Rozdziale VII SWZ warunki udziału w tym postępowaniu. 6. DSZ obowiązywać będzie przez okres 36 miesięcy od dnia jego ustanowienia tj. pierwszej kwalifikacji podmiotowej Wykonawców, którzy złożyli wnioski o dopuszczenie do udziału w DSZ w odpowiedzi na ogłoszenie o zamówieniu lub do wyczerpania maksymalnej szacowanej ilości sprzętu, w zależności od tego, które ze zdarzeń nastąpi wcześniej. 7. Procedury udzielenia zamówień realizacyjnych w ramach ustanowionego DSZ we wszystkich Kategoriach mogą prowadzić na swoją rzecz wszystkie Jednostki wskazane w Wykazie (sądy powszechne, Krajowa Szkoła Sądownictwa i Prokuratury i Centrum Zakupów dla Sądownictwa Instytucja Gospodarki Budżetowej). Ponadto Sądy Apelacyjne mogą prowadzić procedury udzielenia zamówień realizacyjnych w ramach ustanowionego DSZ we wszystkich Kategoriach na rzecz podległych sądów powszechnych, wskazując jako lokalizacje dostaw lokalizacje poszczególnych sądów lub własną lokalizację dostaw. 8. Przewidywane terminy wszczęcia procedur udzielenia zamówień realizacyjnych w okresie obowiązywania DSZ: Zamawiający przewiduje, że: a) zagregowane procedury udzielenia zamówień realizacyjnych o charakterze centralnym, będą prowadzone przez Zamawiającego raz na pół roku, w zależności od realnych potrzeb zgłaszanych przez Jednostki, w szczególności w Kategorii 2, 4 i 6; b) pozostałe procedury udzielenia zamówień realizacyjnych będą prowadzone samodzielnie przez Jednostki - sukcesywnie, w zależności od realnych potrzeb Jednostek, w szczególności w Kategorii 1, 3 i 5. 9. Realizacja dostaw sprzętu objętego DSZ w poszczególnych Kategoriach odbywać się będzie po przeprowadzeniu, za pośrednictwem Systemu, o którym mowa w Rozdziale XII pkt 3 SWZ, procedur udzielenia zamówień realizacyjnych w ramach DSZ, wszczynanych Zaproszeniem do składania ofert skierowanym do wszystkich zakwalifikowanych uczestników DSZ w danej Kategorii. 10. Wykaz Jednostek, na rzecz których prowadzone jest postępowanie oraz uprawnionych do prowadzenia procedur udzielenia zamówień realizacyjnych we wszystkich Kategoriach i udzielania zamówień realizacyjnych zawiera Załącznik nr 9 do SWZ. 11. Pierwszy termin składania wniosków o dopuszczenie do udziału w DSZ w poszczególnych kategoriach, wskazany w SWZ wyznaczono na dzień 13.09.2024r. do godziny 11:00. Po przekazaniu Zaproszenia do składania ofert dotyczących pierwszego zamówienia objętego DSZ, kolejnych terminów na składanie wniosków o dopuszczenie do udziału w DSZ nie wyznacza się. Wykonawca nieobjęty DSZ w danej kategorii może złożyć wniosek w dowolnym czasie obowiązywania DSZ. 12. Kryteria oceny ofert zostały określone w Rozdziale XIV SWZ, przy czym waga wskazanych kryteriów z ramach parametrów technicznych w poszczególnych Kategoriach zostanie sprecyzowana na etapie Zaproszeń do składania ofert w procedurach udzielania zamówień realizacyjnych objętych DSZ 13. Zamawiający informuje, iż na etapie poprzedzającym przygotowanie postępowania, przeprowadził drogą korespondencyjną wstępne konsultacje rynkowe z zainteresowanymi przedstawicielami Producentów, na podstawie art. 84 ustawy z dnia 11 września 2019 r. Prawo zamówień publicznych (tj.: Dz. U. z 2023 r., poz. 1605 z późn. zm.).

Germany – Pharmaceutical products – Abschluss einer nicht-exklusiven Rabattvereinbarung nach § 130a Abs. 8 SGB V zum Wirkstoff Tocilizumab (ausschließlich Infusionslösungskonzentrat), ATC L04AC07 für die Zeit 01.12.2025 - 30.11.2027
description: § 130a Absatz 8 SGB V ermöglicht den Krankenkassen und pharmazeutischen Unternehmen, Rahmenrabattverträge über die zu Lasten der gesetzlichen Krankenkassen abzugebenden Arzneimittel zuschließen. In Hinblick auf die dafür einschlägigen gesetzlichen Vorschriften zur Vergabe öffentlicher Aufträge, findet ein regelmäßiger Prozess wirkstoffbezogener, förmlicher Vergabeverfahren nach den Regularien des 4. Teils des GWB durch die DAK-Gesundheit statt. Für vom Bieter näher in der Anlage 2 zum Vertrag zu benennende Arzneimittel zu dem o. g. Wirkstoff Tocilizumab (ausschließlich Infusionslösungskonzentrat), ATC L04AC07, beabsichtigt die DAK-Gesundheit, bis zum Inkrafttreten neuer Arzneimittelrabattverträge mit möglichst allen interessierten pharmazeutischen Unternehmen Arzneimittelrabattverträge abzuschließen. Ein Rabattvertrag i.R.d. Zulassungsmodells zu dem o. g. Wirkstoff tritt erstmals am 01.12.2025 in Kraft und endet am 30.11.2027. Er endet unabhängig davon automatisch mit Inkrafttreten des Exklusivvertrages.

title: Repair Hush House Concrete B3857
description: The 127 MSC hereby issues a solicitation notice for solicitation W50S8526BA006, a Total Small Business Set-Aside for commercial construction services to repair Hush House concrete at B3857, Project Title VGLZ 262101. This procurement is conducted in accordance with FAR Parts 12, 14, and 36, with an Invitation for Bids (IFB) planned for issuance in the month of July. Classified under Product Service Code (PSC) Z1BD (Maintenance of Airport Runways and Taxiways) and NAICS 237310 (Highway, Runway Construction) with a size standard of $45.0 million, the project magnitude is estimated at less than $1,000,000. The objective of this project is the demolition and replacement of approximately 22,000 square feet of aging Portland Cement Concrete (PCC) pavement at Hush House 3857 and its adjacent approaches. The existing pavement, originally placed in 1983, has exceeded its service life and currently presents a severe Foreign Object Debris (FOD) hazard that poses significant safety risks to personnel and threatens to cause catastrophic damage to aircraft engines, specifically the F-15EX. The scope requires a comprehensive Bid-Build approach to deliver a modernized, unreinforced, airfield-grade PCC surface that meets current military structural and safety standards. All questions or requests for information will be posted to this solicitation notice or incorporated into the solicitation when released. ** ATTACHMENTS CAN BE FOUND IN THE PIEE SOLICITATION MODULE Link noted in the Attachments section. ** AMENDMENT 0001 corrects an administrative error preventing access to the Attachment VGLZ_262101___Combined_Specs. title: USACE SPK DBB Construction - Natomas Reach I Contract 2 - Sacramento, CA
description: The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Sacramento District (SPK) requires design-bid-build (DBB) construction services to be performed in support of the Natomas Reach I Contract 2 (RIC2) at Sacramento, California (CA). The project supports the American River Common Features (ARCF), Natomas Basin Project, located within the great Sacramento region of California. RIC2 is a continuation of Contract 1 which provided cutoff walls for seepage mitigation in the levees for the entire reach of Natomas Reach I, extending from Northgate Boulevard to Gateway Oaks Drive along the American River levee. Contract 2 project requires flattening the landside slope along the American River from Gateway Oaks Drive to the Northgate Boulevard and along the NEMDC. Total length of slope flattening is approximately 2.18 miles and includes site excavation and re-use of approximately 15,000 cubic yard levee embankment fill and borrow site excavation and import of approximately 12,000 cubic yard levee embankment fill. The work also includes the relocation of utilities, construction of a 12-foot maintenance road at the landside toe, and tree removal. Activities that impact the levee prism will only be permitted between 15 April and 1 November. The estimated cost for the project is $10,000,000 to $13,000,000. The Government intends to solicit an Invitation for Bids (IFB) that will result in award of a firm-fixed price contract. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code is 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction. The small business size standard for this NAICS, as established by the United States Small Business Administration (SBA), is $45,500,000.00 annual revenue The Product and Service Code (PSC) is Y1LC, Construction of Tunnels and Subsurface Structures. The solicitation is issued as a total small business set-aside through the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE - https://piee.eb.mil) and Governmentwide Point of Entry, the System for Award Management (SAM - www.SAM.gov).The Government will conduct a pre-bid conference and site walk on 17 August 2026. The solicitation and attachments are posted in Portable Document Format (.pdf) which will require Adobe Acrobat Reader to open and view files. Adobe Acrobat Reader may be downloaded free of charge at http://www.adobe.com/products/reader. All prospective Offerors should be registered in the PIEE system at least one (1) week prior to the anticipated bid due date. Registration is not required to download any forthcoming solicitation documents, plans, and/or specifications, but IS required to submit a bid. Copies of the solicitation and attachments are available for inspection when accessed through PIEE. Failure to register in PIEE will prevent submission of bids as the Government will not accept them by any other means. See linked PIEE registration instructions and web-based training for information about how to access the PIEE Solicitation Module and submit bids. All prospective Offerors must be registered in SAM before the anticipated solicitation closing date. Please see the SAM website for information about SAM registration requirements and approval timelines. USACE will not notify prospective Offerors of any changes to the solicitation; Offerors must monitor PIEE and SAM for the solicitation to be posted, and for any posted changes or amendments. The ONLY Interested Vendors / Plan Holders / Bidders List is available through SAM.gov; Contractors are responsible for identifying their entity as an interested vendor and contacting other interested vendors. USACE SPK will not review capabilities statements submitted in response to this posting or coordinate partnering arrangements between parties. Contractors should check SAM.gov frequently for changes to the interested vendors list and this Notice.--------Amendment 0001 is issued to: 1. title: DOD USAMRDC FY23-FY27 BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT for Extramural Medical Research Department of Defense Dept. of the Army -- USAMRAA
description: The USAMRDC�s mission is to provide solutions to medical problems of importance to the American Service Member at home and abroad, as well as to the general public at large. The scope of this effort and the priorities attached to specific projects are influenced by changes in military and civilian medical science and technology (S&T), operational requirements, military threat assessments, and national defense strategies. Extramural research and development programs play a vital role in the fulfillment of the objectives established by the USAMRDC. General information on the USAMRDC can be obtained at https://mrdc.health.mil/. This BAA is intended to solicit extramural research and development ideas using the authority provided by 10 USC 4001. The BAA is issued under the provisions of the Competition in Contracting Act of 1984 (Public Law 98-369), as implemented in FAR 6.102(d)(2) and 35.016 and in Department of Defense Grant and Agreement Regulations (DoDGARs) 22.315. In accordance with FAR 35.016, projects funded under this BAA must be for basic and applied research to support scientific study and experimentation directed toward advancing the state-of-the-art or increasing knowledge or understanding rather than focusing on development of a specific system or hardware solution. Research and development funded through this BAA are intended and expected to benefit and inform both military and civilian medical practice and knowledge. This BAA utilizes competitive procedures in accordance with 10 USC 2302(2)(B) for the selection for award of S&T proposals/applications. For the purposes of this BAA, S&T includes activities involving basic research, applied research, advanced technology development, and, under certain conditions, may include activities involving advanced component development and prototypes. The selection process is highly competitive, and the quantity of meaningful submissions (both pre-proposals/pre-applications and full proposals/applications) received typically exceeds the number of awards that available funding can support. This BAA provides a general description of USAMRDC�s research and development programs, including Research Areas of Interest, evaluation and selection criteria, pre-proposal/ pre-application and full proposal/application preparation instructions, and general administrative information. Specific submission information and additional administrative requirements can be found in the document titled, �General Submission Instructions,� which is available on Grants.gov along with this BAA. The FY23-FY27 USAMRDC BAA is continuously open for a 5-year period, from October 1, 2022 through September 30, 2027, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time. Submission of a pre-proposal/pre-application is required and must be submitted through the electronic Biomedical Research Application Portal (eBRAP) (https://eBRAP.org/). Pre-proposals/pre-applications may be submitted at any time throughout the 5-year period. If the USAMRDC is interested in receiving a full proposal/application, the Principal Investigator will be sent an invitation to submit via eBRAP. A full proposal/application must be submitted through Grants.gov (http://www.grants.gov/). Invited full proposals/applications can be submitted under this FY23-FY27 BAA through September 30, 2027.

title: Finland – Health and social work services – Osallistumispyyntö: Väestövastuullisen ammatinharjoittajalääkäripalvelun hankinta
description: Hankinnan kohteena on yleislääkäri palveluiden hankinta ammatinharjoittajalääkärimallin mukaiseen työskentelyyn Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialueelle. Hankittavalla palvelulla tuotetaan yleislääkäripalvelut kokonaisvaltaisesti sovitulle vastuuväestölle. Hankittava palvelu sisältää vastaanottokäynnit, etäkontaktit, toimenpiteet, reseptityön, lausunnot, kuntoutussuunnitelmat sekä vastuuväestöä koskeviin muiden ammattilaisten konsultaatioihin vastaamisen. Sopimus on voimassa toistaiseksi ja sopimus astuu voimaan, kun molemmat Osapuolet ovat sen allekirjoittaneet. Tarkempi kuvaus hankinnan sisällöstä on tarjouspyynnön liitteellä 1. "Hankinnan kohteen kuvaus". Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue ei sitoudu tiettyihin hankintamääriin sopimuskauden aikana.

title: Endring av kontrakt, Totalentreprise - 330123/430129 Fredlybekken nedre del etappe 4 Sluppen - styrt boring
description: Trondheim kommune v/ enhet for kommunalteknikk har til hensikt å gjøre endringer i kontrakten Totalentreprise - 330123/430129 Fredlybekken nedre del etappe 4 Sluppen - styrt boring (Doffin ID: 2023-697427) iht. forsyningsforskriften § 24-1 første ledd bokstav d).Trondheim kommune og Søbstad AS inngikk i september 2023 kontrakt om totalentreprise for Fredlybekken, hvor opprinnelig spesifisert gjennomføringsmetode for no-dig-arbeidene var styrt boring. Som følge av krevende, uforutsette grunnforhold ble metoden i første omgang forsøkt endret til pilotrørsboring i starten av 2026.Etter gjentatte mislykkede forsøk i våren 2026, samt påvisning av svært vanskelige og uforutsette grunnforhold med blant annet rasmasser og varierte løsmasser, viser faglige vurderinger at verken styrt boring eller pilotrørsboring lar seg gjennomføre. Til tross for omfattende grunnundersøkelser og grundige tekniske vurderinger av byggherre, totalentreprenør, underentreprenører, rådgivere og eksterne eksperter innenfor fagfeltet har ingen av de valgte metodene lyktes i å få etablert spillvannsrøret. For å sikre at ledningsanlegget blir ferdigstilt i henhold til kontraktens funksjonskrav, er det nødvendig å endre gjennomføringsmetoden til mikrotunnelering med lukket front for de gjenstående no-dig-arbeidene for etablering av spillvannsledningen.Endringen vurderes som tillatt etter forsyningsforskriften § 24-1 første ledd bokstav d da følgende tre vilkår er oppfylt:Endringen er nødvendig:Metodeendringen til tunnelering er strengt nødvendig for at oppdragsgiver skal få oppfylt kontraktens formål og sikre planlagt funksjonalitet for overvanns- og spillvannsledningene. For å sikre at kostnadene ved endringen holdes på et nødvendig og konkurransedyktig nivå, har entreprenøren gjennomført en konkurranse for tunneleringen.Uforutsette omstendigheter:Behovet for endringen skyldes grunnforhold som en aktsom oppdragsgiver ikke kunne forutse ved inngåelsen av kontrakten. Det ble utført grundige grunnundersøkelser i ulik format, både før oppstart og underveis i prosjektet. Omfanget av de uforutsette, inhomogene rasmassene og blokksteinene i grunnen var det likevel ikke mulig å avdekke før arbeidet var satt i gang.Anskaffelsens overordnede karakter endres ikke:Endringen gjelder kun den tekniske utførelsesmetoden for en del av no-dig-traseen. Hovedytelsen, kontraktens formål, ansvars- og risikofordelingen forblir uendret.Vilkårene i forsyningsforskriften § 24-1 første ledd bokstav d er oppfylt. Endringen kunngjøres i henhold til forsyningsforskriften § 24-1 tredje ledd, jf. § 17.1.

While white papers will be considered if received prior to 0500 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 Sep 2027, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY23 by 2 Mar 2023 FY24 by 15 September 2023 FY25 by 15 September 2024 FY26 by 15 September 2025 FY27 by 15 September 2026 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Today�s aerial layer �network� architecture requires significant pre-planning and has limited interoperability. AFRL desires innovations to move from this current state to a significantly more on demand, self-forming, self-healing aerial layer network. Research in network monitoring and management, robust aerial networks, and proof of concept capabilities are sought to advance this objective. This BAA is a follow-on to BAA FA8750-19-S-7001 entitled �Timely, Secure & Mission Responsive Aerial Warfighting Network Capabilties�. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99.5M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 36 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $1M to $10M. There is also the potential to make awards up to $49.5M. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more Procurement Contracts, Other Transactions, or assistance instruments, for all, some ,or none of the solicited effort based on the offeror�s ability to perform desired work and funding fluctuations. There is no limit on the number of OTs that may be awarded to an individual offeror. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: FAR based Procurement contracts, DODGARS based grants and cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) under 10 USC 4021, 10 USC 4022 and 10 USC 4023 (previously 10 USC 4003, 2371, 10 USC 4003, 2371b and 4004, 2373) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Timothy Weaver AFRL/RITGA 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315)330-2958 Email: timothy.weaver.16@us.af.mil <mailto:timothy.weaver.16@us.af.mil> Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below (email requests are preferred): Amber Buckley Telephone (315) 330-3605 Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil <mailto:Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil> Emails must reference the solicitation BAA number and title of the acquisition. Pre-Proposal Communication between Prospective Offerors and Government Representatives: Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is encouraged. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. Offerors are cautioned that evaluation ratings may be lowered and/or proposal rejected if proposal preparation (Proposal format, content, etc.) and/or submittal instructions are not followed.
